newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Filipino group protests visit by Singapore's Goh.
newsitem.headline: Filipino group protests visit by Singapore's Goh.

text.p: Filipino workers, angry at the hanging of a Filipina maid in Singapore two years ago, denounced Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong as an "executioner" on Monday in a rally outside his country's embassy.
Goh was to arrive in the Philippines on Monday to try to boost relations which were damaged by the hanging in Singapore of Flor Contemplacion for murder.

"The two governments are best remembered as the ones who murdered Flor Contemplacion -- the Philippine government's (inability) and the Singaporean government's malevolence led to the barbaric death," rally leader Imelda Lauindam said.
About 20 members of the Migrante International workers group held a peaceful protest against the visit, which one local newspaper called "a meeting between despotism and democracy".
Contemplacion was hanged in 1995 after confessing to killing another Filipina maid and a Singaporean boy in the maid's care.
Despite autopsy findings backing the Singapore case, many Filipinos believe Contemplacion was a victim of a frame-up and burned Singaporean flags in nationwide protests at the time.
The uproar forced Goh to cancel his Manila visit scheduled that year as the two countries came to a near diplomatic break.
"I hope with my coming visit, we should be able to restore the momentum to (its) previous level," Goh said last week.
A Philippine presidential palace news release said talks between Goh and President Fidel Ramos would focus on trade, investments and strengthening of Manila-Singapore ties.
Goh will address a business group and visit the former U.S. Clark air base which Manila has turned into an industrial complex.
